title: S1 bootstrap: pull branch, queue season jobs, pull bc01 numbers
prompt:
You are the Mac worker (Vijenders-MacBook-Pro.local) with full edit rights per CLAUDE.md. Do these steps IN ORDER and report each in your result.

1. PULL THE BRANCH: git fetch origin claude/ai-unpacked-vj-analytics-9lhetq. If the working tree is dirty, run `git stash --include-untracked` first and say so in the result. Then `git checkout claude/ai-unpacked-vj-analytics-9lhetq && git pull --ff-only origin claude/ai-unpacked-vj-analytics-9lhetq`. This brings in the Season 1 restructure (BUILD-CLUB.md section 4), scripts/enqueue_job.py, and deploy/restart_worker.sh.

2. QUEUE THE SEASON PRODUCE JOB (bc02, Mon Aug 17): run `python3 scripts/enqueue_job.py produce_short --channel claude-tricks --model sonnet --effort low --calendar-date 2026-08-17 --title "Ch.2 — Make Your Website SMART (One AI Move) 🧠" --prompt "SEASON 1 Mon chapter (bc02, calendar row bc02, season bible BUILD-CLUB.md section 4). Opens on the LIVE bc01 site youtu.be/bWoa98zMWjA build (standalone-first, point legible in 2s). Claude adds ONE free AI feature to the live site on camera; after the feature lands, type 'What am I missing?' in the same session and let the answer harden the build (folded ep19 move). Verify the chosen free AI-embed path is current at production. Homework outro: add yours + comment SHIPPED. Season promise on screen: started Monday, listed by Thursday. Pass ALL 5 Audition Gates (BUILD-CLUB.md section 7) before arm. Slot 2026-08-17 16:00 IST = 10:30 UTC."` — if enqueue_job.py exits 2 (no factory_calendar row for 2026-08-17), re-run the same command WITHOUT --calendar-date and note that in the result.

3. QUEUE THE bc01 RETENTION READ: run `python3 scripts/enqueue_job.py custom --channel claude-tricks --model sonnet --effort low --title "BC01 retention read (bWoa98zMWjA) vs season thresholds" --prompt "Run: python3 scripts/yt_retention.py --channel claude-tricks --video bWoa98zMWjA --summary --md docs/stats/RETENTION.md. Then read the result against the pre-committed d0 thresholds in docs/stats/AI-UNPACKED-READ-2026-08-14.md section 4 (>=90 keep / 20-90 hold+fix hook / <20 format question) and state which band bc01 landed in and where the curve drops. Also run: python3 scripts/yt_engage.py --channel claude-tricks --video bWoa98zMWjA --count-keyword SHIPPED --days 7. Commit docs/stats/RETENTION.md to the current branch and push with git push -u origin claude/ai-unpacked-vj-analytics-9lhetq."`

4. REFRESH STATS NOW: run `python3 scripts/network_stats.py` (tokens live on this Mac). Then commit docs/stats/history.csv + docs/stats/DAILY-STATS.md to the current branch and push. This captures bc01's first real post-publish numbers.

5. QUEUE THE WORKER RESTART LAST (after everything else is queued and pushed): run `python3 scripts/enqueue_job.py shell_script --channel claude-tricks --title "restart worker (load usage rollup)" --prompt "restart per deploy/restart_worker.sh" --meta '{"script_path": "deploy/restart_worker.sh"}'` (the pulled enqueue_job.py has the --meta flag). The restart kills this worker's process tree and launchd relaunches it with the pulled code (usage rollup lands in factory_workers.meta.usage) — the restart job itself gets reaped as orphaned afterwards, which is EXPECTED and documented in deploy/restart_worker.sh. Note: if the restart job runs while YOUR job is still alive it would kill you too — so queue it as your very last action before writing your result.

6. RESULT: list what got queued (job ids), the network_stats headline for AI Unpacked (bc01 views so far), and any step that deviated.
